inlines.v: RAPA'CIOUS, adjective [Latin rapax, from rapio, to seize. See Rap.] 1. Given to plunder; disposed or accustomed to seize by violence; seizing by force; as a rapacious enemy. Well may thy lord, appeas'd redeem thee quite from death's rapacious claim. 2. Accustomed to seize for food; subsisting on prey or animals seized by violence; as a rapacious tiger; a rapacious fowl.
